decisions.reason: The source adds explicit short-edge accessibility constraints for J_BAT and USB-C to the active integrated-board connector-access requirement.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
some constraints I can think of:

Constraints regardless of orientation:
\- J\_BAT on a short edge (battery sits alongside PCB)
\- USB-C on a short edge (user-facing)
\- Display connectors (J\_DISP\_SPI / J\_DISP\_I2C / J\_DISP\_LED) grouped together on the edge closest to where the display flex will route
\- ESP32-S3 antenna end facing away from battery, ≥3mm keepout

decisions.reason: The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY recording the antenna orientation, 3 mm keepout, and integrated-board scope.
The source constrains connectors on the integrated board and does not reinstate or alter the already eliminated legacy interboard-alignment behavior.
Physical connector placement does not change the established single-board architecture or board count.
The source specifies connector and antenna placement but makes no decision about the legacy main-board layer count.
The orientation-independent connector constraints do not establish new dimensions or alter the legacy main-board fit and routing state.
The source changes physical placement constraints only; it does not alter the cost goal, component-selection policy, architecture, or connector-count strategy.
Grouping display connectors affects integrated-board layout but does not change the required sensor connector fanout, connector types, signals, or consolidation policy.
Locating USB-C on a user-facing short edge does not change native USB data lines, sourceability, enumeration, or programming behavior.
The physical grouping of J_DISP_LED with the other display connectors does not alter its load on the switchable 5 V rail or any boost-control behavior.
The location of J_DISP_I2C does not change I2C speed, pull-ups, series resistors, topology, or signal-conditioning requirements.
The USB-C edge placement does not change the standalone regulator, activation condition, powered rail, source selection, or programming support.
